source_context: After receiver-validating the structural theorem that Q(zeta_8)/Q has exactly three quadratic intermediate fields, GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT continued on a stacked integration branch. The accepted prerequisite modules already provide the concrete fields generated by sqrt(2), sqrt(-2), and i. This slice proves those three fields are pairwise distinct by showing every pair generates the full degree-four cyclotomic field, and then combines pairwise distinctness with the previously validated cardinality-three theorem to prove that every quadratic intermediate field is one of the three classical fields. The first receiver run compiled and kernel-checked the mathematics but rejected the raw exhaustion statement because its normalized type was 98,663 bytes, above the 65,536-byte limit. The producer therefore changed the exhaustion theorem to accept the already-defined compact subtype CyclotomicEightQuadraticFields, which carries exactly the same degree-two hypothesis without re-elaborating the large IntermediateField module structure. A subsequent receiver run built and kernel-checked the compact theorem successfully but failed only because the claim metadata still named an obsolete experimental entrypoint; this claim now names the actual audited theorem. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected and authored the statements and proofs; the human did not author or materially edit the Lean text. No claim of new mathematics is made.
